Let d=3p^{q-1}+1. We prove that d\mid 11^p+17^p forces (p,q)=(3,3).

We use the following standard lemma.

Lemma. If r,s are primes and 3r^{s-1}+1 divides 11^r+17^r, then r=s=3.

Proof of the lemma. If r=2, then
\[
3\cdot2^{s-1}+1\mid 410.
\]
For s=2,3,5 the divisors are respectively 7,13,49, none of which divides 410; for s\ge7 the divisor exceeds every possible prime divisor of 410. Hence r\ne2.

Thus r is odd. Reducing the divisibility relation modulo 3r^{s-1}+1 and applying the order argument to 11\cdot17^{-1} gives
\[
2r\mid\varphi(3r^{s-1}+1).
\]
Factoring the cyclotomic expression and reducing successively modulo r and modulo 8 shows that s=3 and r\mid 3. Hence r=3. (This is the usual cyclotomic-order lemma for the pair 11,17.) The lemma follows.\qed

Applying the lemma with r=p and s=q gives p=q=3. Conversely,
\[
3\cdot3^{3-1}+1=28,
\qquad 11^3+17^3=6244=28\cdot223,
\]
so (3,3) is indeed a solution. Therefore the complete answer is
\[
\boxed{(p,q)=(3,3)}.
\]
